clue.text: Having to dress several can be wearying

parts.note: to tire is an old word for to attire or dress
some means an indefinite few, several

explanation.surface: Having to get a whole crowd of people dressed is exhausting work.
explanation.walkthrough: TIRE is the archaic verb behind 'attire', still met in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that wears you out is tedious and fatiguing, a synonym pair.

clue.text: The endless rush gets the bird

indicators.note: endless means the word The loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rush of people without end ends in someone being booed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' sounds like being jeered, but 'the bird' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrush is a songbird, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: One dares to rebel when promoted

indicators.note: to rebel is to break ranks and refuse order, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
taken as written

explanation.surface: A daring person decides to revolt after being given a higher post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rebel' rearranges I (One) and DARES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone promoted has been lifted up in rank, a synonym.

clue.text: Almost dropped in to report guardedly

indicators.note: in means the shortened word goes inside the word for report

parts.note: to report is to say

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is cut from the word for dropped

parts.note: fell means dropped, as a past tense

explanation.surface: Someone nearly collapses in while coming to give an account carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims FELL to FEL; 'in' puts FEL inside SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with caution and protection means doing things without risk, a synonym.

clue.text: Well he's just avoiding work!

parts.note: read as an exasperated complaint, but 'Well' also means healthy: here is a perfectly healthy man who shirks his job by pretending to be ill

explanation.surface: An exasperated boss grumbles that an employee is simply dodging his duties.
explanation.definitionFit: A shirker who feigns sickness while actually healthy fits the description of someone fit but skiving.

clue.text: Away result causing disgust

parts.note: off means away, as in going off
the end is the outcome or result

explanation.surface: An away fixture ends in a result that leaves fans revolted.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a football away result; 'causing' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To disgust someone is to affront or upset them, a synonym.

clue.text: Following decline, a European intended to raise the standard

indicators.note: following means the European comes after the word for decline

parts.note: to flag is to tire or decline
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: After a slump, a European is determined to lift the level of achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' is a flag, not a level of quality; the definition describes what the mast is for.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall mast exists so that a banner can be hoisted on it.

clue.text: Expulsion for getting into vice possibly

indicators.note: possibly means the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is thrown out for falling into wicked ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges INTO and VICE together; 'for getting' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Being forced out of a home by a landlord is a kind of ejection.

clue.text: Become less smooth

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to take the creases out, as with an iron

explanation.definitionFit: Shrink in amount, and also, playfully, remove wrinkles from cloth.

clue.text: A comedown for the artist in autumn

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual artist
taken as written
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: A painter suffers a setback during the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A comedown' looks like a disappointment, but it describes what drops from the clouds.
explanation.definitionFit: Water from the sky literally descends, so it is wittily something that comes down.

clue.text: The person in charge restraining a frenzied individual

parts.note: a man is a person

indicators.note: restraining means the letters for in charge hold the a inside them

explanation.surface: The boss is holding back a person who has gone wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restraining' puts A inside IC to make IAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildly unstable person behaving with frenzy is a madman.

clue.text: Drink in support, though it's antisocial behaviour

indicators.note: in means the drink is placed inside the word for support

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm
tea is a drink

explanation.surface: Having a drink while wearing an arm brace, though it is somehow considered bad behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft is a crime against others, an example of antisocial conduct.

clue.text: Quarrel with a fellow-a bit of a bloomer

parts.note: a spat is a minor quarrel
he refers to a male, a fellow

explanation.surface: Arguing with a man turns out to be something of a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake; here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bract enclosing a flower cluster, as on an arum lily, is part of a flowering plant.

clue.text: Appearing, not for the first time, to be concerned with 19

definitions.text: Appearing, not for the first time

parts.note: re means concerning or about
19 down is the word for entry, and entry means entrance

explanation.surface: Coming on stage again turns out to be connected with the entry clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 refers to the answer of 19 down, whose sense 'entry' supplies ENTRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming back on to the stage a second time is a repeated arrival.

clue.text: Ordering beer left many debts not easily settled

indicators.note: ordering means putting these letters into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword many
IOUs are written promises to pay, so they stand for debts

explanation.surface: A drinker running up a big bar tab finds the bill hard to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordering' rearranges BEER and L into REBEL; L (many, fifty) and IOUS follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Unruly and defiant people are hard to calm or bring into line.

clue.text: Obeyed and kept watch

definitions.meaning: followed a rule, as in respected the law

explanation.definitionFit: Complied with a rule, and also looked at attentively.

clue.text: Curious trait of Cyrano de Bergerac?

definitions.text: Curious trait of Cyrano de Bergerac?

parts.words: Curious trait of Cyrano de Bergerac?
parts.note: curious means inquisitive, a prying habit, but Cyrano is the play's hero famed for his enormous nose, so the trait is also being very nosed

explanation.surface: A question about an odd characteristic of the famous French swordsman-poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyrano de Bergerac, from Rostand's play, is known for his huge nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Prying inquisitiveness is the trait, with a pun on having a big nose.

clue.text: Act up over a number in the pits getting what's left

indicators.note: over means the reversed piece sits above the rest in this down entry
up in a down clue means the word for act is read from the bottom

parts.note: to do is to act

indicators.note: in means the number goes inside the word for the pits

parts.note: dents are small pits or hollows
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Misbehaving over a figure while stuck in the depths, someone ends up with the remnants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DO into OD; 'in' puts M inside DENTS; 'over' stacks OD above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftover scraps and remnants are what remains after the rest is used.

clue.text: Leguminous food widely available?

parts.note: leguminous food means pulses, and widely available suggests beans that are spread far, or broadly, giving a wide variety of bean

explanation.surface: A question about whether a type of pulse is easy to obtain.
explanation.definitionFit: Large flat pulses eaten as a vegetable, playfully called beans that are wide.

clue.text: Credit entry

definitions.meaning: a way in, as in gaining admittance

explanation.walkthrough: Access was a well-known UK credit card from 1972 to 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: A former British credit card name, and also a means of getting in.

clue.text: The big gun is able to point forward

parts.note: can means is able
N, north, is a point of the compass
on means forward, as in moving on

explanation.surface: The important person is able to lead the way ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The big gun' looks like a VIP, but it is literal artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: A large piece of artillery is a heavy weapon that fires shot.

clue.text: Bar set up outside a show

indicators.note: outside means the turned word for bar goes around a
set up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lever is a metal bar used to prise

explanation.surface: A pub is set up beside an exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns LEVER into REVEL; 'outside' puts it round A.
explanation.definitionFit: To display or disclose something is to make it visible, a synonym.

clue.text: Half of them gain surprisingly-such a mystery

indicators.note: surprisingly means the letters fall into an unexpected order
half of means only the latter part of the word them is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting half of them would be a puzzling outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes EM, the back half of 'them'; 'surprisingly' rearranges EM and GAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle or riddle that baffles people is a mystery, a synonym.

clue.text: Carry on without concern for devastation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for carry on goes around

parts.note: to wage is to carry on, as in wage war
reck is an old word for care or concern

explanation.surface: Keep going regardless of the destruction around you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, putting WAGE round RECK; RECK survives in 'reckless'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruined remains after a disaster are the result of destruction.

clue.text: A city girl returning after six

indicators.note: after means the girl's name comes behind six

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: returning means the girl's name runs backwards

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl comes back to town after six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ANNE into ENNA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian capital is an example of a city.

clue.text: They feel Article 10-key article to be retrogressive

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
ten is 10

indicators.note: to be retrogressive means the last two pieces go backwards

parts.note: E is a musical key
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Readers feel that Article 10 being a key clause would be a backward step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be retrogressive' turns E and AN into NAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects use their feelers to sense surroundings, so they do the feeling.

clue.text: To stop the use of some insecticides is thought advisable

indicators.note: some means only part of the run of words insecticides is thought is used

explanation.surface: Banning some pesticides is considered sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'insecticiDES IS Thought'; 'the use of' and 'advisable' only dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease or refrain from an action is a synonym pair.

clue.text: A sale's on maybe only at a particular time of year

definitions.text: only at a particular time of year

indicators.note: maybe means the letters might be put together differently

explanation.surface: A sale is happening, possibly only during a certain season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges all the letters of A SALES ON, counting the S of sale's.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens at a certain point in the calendar is tied to the time of year.
